title: Streamed JSON repair, escape-scaffold, and idempotent tool-retry policy
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Teams are seeing malformed or truncated JSON objects when the generator streams structured output across network boundaries or when client-driven truncation occurs. Tool/function calls intertwined with streaming exacerbate rebuild complexity because a partial tool invocation payload can lead to duplicate side-effects when retried. Current heuristics (simple bracket balancing) are insufficient for nested objects, escaped strings, and interleaved tool-call frames.

Goals:
- Define a lightweight, runtime-friendly repair strategy that can reconstruct or safely truncate streamed JSON objects without silently corrupting intent.
- Provide a deterministic escape-scaffold that preserves parsability of partial outputs and allows clients to resume or fallback with minimal state.
- Create idempotent retry semantics for tool/function calls emitted mid-stream, preventing duplicate side-effects while preserving developer ergonomics.
- Integrate with backpressure/truncation policies so the repair strategy works under aggressive latency SLOs and token caps.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Stream chunk metadata: emit a tiny ASCII token header on chunk boundaries when structured output mode enabled. Header is reversible and non-ambiguous (example: "<<RI-CHUNK v1 meta=...>>\n"). It contains: chunk-seq, object-depth-snapshot, last-escape-state, optional idempotency-hash for any tool call emitted in that chunk.
2) Escape scaffold: when the model emits an incomplete string (ends in unmatched \" or trailing backslash), we insert a deterministic scaffold sequence that signals \"partial-string\" rather than attempting to close or escape client-visible content. Client SDKs should strip scaffolds on successful full output but use them to detect truncation boundaries. Example scaffold: "\uE000_PARTIAL_STR\uE001" (uses private Unicode plane to avoid collision).
3) Repair rules: runtime will apply rules in order on truncated streams: a) consult chunk header object-depth-snapshot to re-open necessary brackets, b) if last-escape-state indicates open string, append closing quote and mark as truncated=true, c) if idempotency-hash present for a tool call, attach a retry token to the tool invocation so downstream systems can dedupe. The runtime will never fabricate new keys or change values beyond insertion of a special \"__TRUNCATED\": true marker at the deepest truncated object.
4) Tool/function idempotency: every tool call emitted in-stream must include an idempotency token computed from (request_id, call_index, model-seed). If the runtime retries a chunk or the client replays, the tool backend must accept the token and dedupe side-effects. We will provide SDK wrappers and a fallback policy that converts non-idempotent tool calls into validated \"dry-run + confirm\" sequences when backend does not support dedupe.
5) Client/backpressure contract: when truncation occurs because of token_limit, runtime will attempt a graceful short-circuit: close any open JSON containers using scaffold rules, append \"__TRUNCATED\": true, and emit a final chunk header with truncated=true and an optional resume_cursor that the model can use for a follow-up request.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- We avoid binary manifests per chunk to keep tokens low; ASCII headers are small and easy to detect.
- Using private Unicode scalars for scaffold minimizes collisions with user content while being removable by SDKs.
- We prefer conservative repair (mark truncated) vs. optimistic repair (guess missing values) to avoid silent misinterpretation in downstream tooling and audits.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Runtime emits chunk headers and scaffolds when structured_output mode is enabled (feature flag).
2) SDKs (JS/Python/Go) can detect scaffolds and present a consistent API: onPartial, onComplete, onTruncated with resume_cursor.
3) Tool calls include idempotency tokens and the runtime can attach retry metadata when re-emitting a chunk.
4) Integration tests cover: nested objects with escaped strings, truncation mid-UTF8 rune, tool-call in middle of object, client-driven early termination, and dedupe behavior against a mock tool backend.
5) Performance overhead must be <0.75% p99 token latency for typical requests (100-1000 token responses) when headers/scaffolds enabled.

Notes on compatibility layer:
- Provide a compatibility shim that translates legacy bracket-balance heuristics to the new header+scaffold approach for older clients until SDKs roll out.
- Expose an opt-in server-side configuration to toggle \"aggressive repair\" for teams who prefer best-effort reconstructions.

Related artifacts: design doc, proto sketch, and test harness links below in attachments.

1) Chunk headers and scaffold emitted under structured_output feature flag.
2) SDK surface: onPartial/onComplete/onTruncated with resume_cursor.
3) Idempotency token present for every tool invocation; mock backend dedupes.
4) Integration tests for nested escapes, truncation at rune boundary, and tool-call retry dedupe.
